purpose: The authoritative Forge->Legion(Arcane) schema mapping S00 deferred (S00-REPORT.md line 47: 'no canonical target mapping was produced ... mark mapping as deferred to S01'). Every legacy semantic item that can affect signoff, authority, invalidation, or compatibility carries an explicit disposition. Nothing is left unresolved; nothing legacy is laundered into trust.

dispositionVocabulary.canonical: Maps onto a named field of a frozen Legion contract. The value carries forward with its meaning intact.
dispositionVocabulary.compatibility-only: Preserved verbatim inside legacy-envelope-v1.payload for legacy readers. Has no canonical meaning and MUST NOT be read by canonical Legion code.
dispositionVocabulary.deprecated: Preserved in the envelope payload, but no canonical successor exists and none is planned. Legacy callers keep working; new callers must not use it.
dispositionVocabulary.rejected: Explicitly refused. The legacy field asserts a trust, authority, or invalidation property Forge did not actually establish. Importing it as-is would weaken Legion (S01 action 4: 'never silently weaken'). Reason is recorded per field.

globalRules: R1 — Every imported legacy record is wrapped in legacy-envelope-v1 with provenance.authenticated == false (the schema pins it to const:false). No import path can produce an authenticated legacy record.

R2 — Trust class, attestation, check status, and authority values are NEVER carried across as canonical facts. They are compatibility-only or rejected. Canonical trust is re-derived by S03 (authentication) and S04 (host-observed effects), never inherited.
R3 — Legacy runs are read without destructive rewrite (S01 action 5). This mapping describes a projection, not a migration that mutates the source store.

R4 — Legacy run ids are UUIDv4 and do not match the ids.md opaque-handle grammar. They are never rewritten in place; correspondence is recorded as an explicit legacyId<->canonicalId pair minted through the Kernel identity interface (S01 action 2). Arcane maintains no private allocator — see lib/kernel-binding.mjs.
R5 — Where a legacy behavior conflicts with a stronger Legion invariant, the conflict surfaces as a typed compatibility error, not a silent downgrade (S01 action 4).

legacyRunId.mechanism: Recorded as legacy-envelope-v1.payload.id plus an explicit correspondence pair emitted by lib/legacy-bridge.mjs. The canonical run id is minted through kernel-binding.mintId('run'); while the Kernel lane is unlanded the minted id is flagged provisional:true and no canonical state write occurs (writes fail closed with ARC_KERNEL_PRIMITIVE_UNAVAILABLE).
legacyRunId.note: S01 action 2 forbids a private ID allocator. This is the seam that honors it.

legacyTaskId.canonicalForm: ktask_<ulid> (Kernel) — ExecutionTask T-#.# is a different object

legacySessionId.canonicalForm: no canonical Legion field; carried on the Arcane replay scope only

legacyWorkspaceHash.note: shape differs (bare hash vs sha256: prefix) — bridge normalizes to sha256:<hex> or records null.

recordTypes.primaryCanonicalTarget: legion-run-identity-v1 (+ legion-execution-contract-v1 for the acceptance/criteria half)
recordTypes.note: A Forge 'run' fuses two Legion objects: a run identity (workspace/revision binding) and a fragment of an execution contract (acceptance criteria, blast radius). Neither half survives as a whole; fields are dispositioned individually.

fields.note: string<=2000; objective requires minLength 1.
Forge routing hint; Legion routes by contract + latitude, not by task_kind.
Legacy entries are free strings with no AC-# id; the bridge assigns positional AC-<n> ids and records that the ids are bridge-assigned, not Sage-authored.

fields.reason: Legacy enum model|host|hook|operator is a caller-supplied string on a store row. S00 confirmed no code path in Forge ever mints 'hook' or 'operator' (inventory compatibility_and_authority_frozen_facts), and 'host' is granted at connection level once at MCP startup, not per message (S00 finding 2). Canonical authority is asserted by Arcane's Kernel binding per turn; lib/authority.mjs owns enforcement. A legacy value is never promoted to a canonical authority assertion.

fields.note: Forge 'strong' default is an enforcement-strength label the code never verified. Canonical enforcement health is computed, not declared — see ENFORCEMENT_LEVEL in lib/errors.mjs.

Lossy in one direction: a legacy 'closed' run that was blocked at its gate is still status='closed'; the bridge therefore consults the run's close decision row before choosing COMPLETED vs FAILED_INVOCATION.
Legion budget/stop conditions live on execution-contract-v1.stopConditions as declared prose; the numeric Forge budget object has no canonical successor.
Normalized to sha256:<hex>; null when Forge stored a non-conforming value.
Part of Forge's high_risk gate triple.
Rubrics have no canonical Legion object; see recordTypes.rubrics.

hashValue(rubric) of the rubric snapshot verify() happened to see. Safe to keep non-canonical because Legion re-derives gate outcomes from canonical evidence at read time (see operation-map verify.conflicts) — an inherited rubric version would only assert that some past gate ran, never that it would pass now.

A past verification timestamp is provenance, not freshness. Canonical freshness is recomputed by the S05 dependency ledger against every bound dimension, so inheriting this value cannot make stale evidence look current.
This is the one legacy field that genuinely encodes a dependency binding; it becomes a dependency edge, not a verdict.

fields.reason_not_canonical: A ledger hash computed by the same process that wrote the ledger is integrity-at-capture, not tamper evidence against that process. Arcane's own chain (lib/receipt-store.mjs) replaces it.

fields.note: store-layer bookkeeping added by lib/store.js on read.
store-layer bookkeeping.

recordTypes.note: Forge 'claims' are epistemic assertions about the world (hypothesis/local_fact/...). Legion claims are authority-scoped release claims (ROOT_CAUSE_ESTABLISHED, CONTROL_PASS, ...), owned by the contracts and Arcane claim boundary. These are DIFFERENT OBJECTS that share an English word. The mapping is therefore deliberately shallow: a Forge claim becomes evidence-shaped context, never a Legion claim.

fields.note: Projection is lossy and one-way; the original kind stays on the envelope payload.
Legion severity lives on Oracle findings, not on evidence.

fields.reason: status='supported' on a Forge claim was reachable from non-model authority whose only proof was an unauthenticated receipt (S00 finding 5). Importing 'supported' would grant Legion-side support that was never established. All legacy claims import with no canonical support; CLAIM_BOUNDARY is recomputed from canonical evidence only. status='stale' IS honored — staleness is a safe direction to inherit (never un-stales anything).

fields.note: An opaque caller-chosen string in Forge (S00 finding 4). It maps to a dependency ref with dimension 'opaque-legacy-key', which the S05 ledger treats as an unresolvable dependency: it can stale things, it can never prove freshness.

fields.reason: A self-reported numeric confidence has no canonical role: Legion states evidence class and staleness, not model confidence.

A legacy waiver was authorized by 'non-model authority', i.e. by the same connection-level trust S00 finding 2 shows is not per-message. Waiver authority in Legion is a policy-named authority (policy/arcane-policy-v1.json waiverAuthority); legacy waivers import as historical annotations that grant nothing.

recordTypes.note: The highest-risk mapping in this document. Forge evidence carries three trust-bearing fields (trust_class, attested, attestation_reason) that Legion must not inherit.

fields.note: Digest preserved as a digest only (S03 action 9). Already in sha256:<hex> form.

fields.reason: trust_class='tool' is assigned purely from the caller's authority string (lib/core.js:486-500), and for authority='host' that string is backed by connection-level trust plus an unvalidated non-empty receipt string (S00 finding 5). Importing 'tool' would create qualifying evidence out of nothing. Every imported legacy evidence row is unauthenticated by construction (legacy-envelope-v1.provenance.authenticated const:false). Canonical evidence class is assigned by the bridge from the claim-kind projection, never from trust_class. Note also the S00-flagged inconsistency that official_doc/verifier/user are readable by verify.js but never assignable by core.js.

attested=true means only that Forge re-hashed a locator file at some past moment. It is not authentication and not freshness. Canonical freshness is the S05 dependency ledger's answer, recomputed at read time.

fields.note: Retained verbatim because the negative reasons (outside_workspace, unreadable_locator, excerpt_not_in_source, symbol_not_in_source) are genuinely useful provenance. The positive ones (verified_against_source, host_receipt) are NOT treated as trust.

Inherited ONLY in the true direction. stale=true imports as stale=true; stale=false imports as stale=true anyway, because Forge's staleness was never computed against the Legion dependency set. Staleness is monotone on import.

Free-text explanation attached to a legacy stale flag. Safe as compatibility-only because staleness is monotone on import (see evidence.stale): the reason can never un-stale anything, it only annotates why Forge thought so.
Superseded by policy/arcane-policy-v1.json evidence.freshness.
Content, not a digest. Subject to policy/arcane-policy-v1.json retention rules on import.

Criterion linkage is re-established canonically by the S05 dependency ledger (link(evidenceId,{criterionId})), which binds evidence to a criterion only when the declared evidence method matches (S04 action 7). An inherited criterion id therefore names a relationship, never satisfies one.

Criterion linkage is re-established canonically by the S05 dependency ledger (link(evidenceId,{criterionId})), which binds evidence to a criterion only when the declared evidence method matches (S04 action 7). An inherited criterion id therefore names a relationship, never satisfies one.

fields.canonicalTarget: artifact-v1.sensitivity (when the evidence materializes an artifact)

fields.note: Same as evidence.criterion_id: the link is re-derived canonically. A legacy check id pointing at a criterion cannot make that criterion proven, because the check itself imports with no canonical proof (see checks.status).

Same as evidence.criterion_id: the link is re-derived canonically. A legacy check id pointing at a criterion cannot make that criterion proven, because the check itself imports with no canonical proof (see checks.status).

fields.reason: Derived from the caller's own authority string (lib/core.js:527-535). Canonical executor identity comes from the host event (S04), never from the record being imported.

Identical defect to runs.authority: a caller-supplied string on a store row, where host authority was granted once at connection level rather than per message (S00 finding 2), and hook/operator were never minted by any Forge code path at all. Canonical authority is kernel-asserted per turn. See globalRules R2.

THE central S00 finding-5 case. status='passed' is reachable under authority='host' by attaching any non-empty string to check.receipt, whose exit_status is parsed with zero structural validation (lib/core.js:536-539). A legacy passing check therefore proves nothing and imports as no canonical proof at all. Forge's own conservative behavior — model authority is FORCED to status='failed' (lib/core.js:540-542, 'model cannot self-certify a passing check') — is preserved and generalized: no imported check ever yields canonical proof, regardless of its legacy authority.

fields.note: Carried as an observation, never as a verdict. S04 acceptance: 'irrelevant exit 0 never proves a criterion'.

fields.reason: Free-form string trusted unconditionally when authority='host' (lib/core.js:493-494,536-539). This is exactly what S04 exists to close. Imported only as opaque envelope payload with authenticated:false; it can never satisfy verifyRecord.

recordTypes.note: Forge 'decisions' are gate outcomes, not Sage decisions (D-#). No canonical object corresponds. They are historical audit rows.

fields.note: Projection onto ALCHEMIST_STATE/DOMAIN_OUTCOME. Lossy: 'proceed' and 'closed' both land on COMPLETE.
signoff|high_risk|null. Canonical gating is policy-driven (policy/arcane-policy-v1.json claimLevels), not a two-value gate name.

fields.reason: Identical defect to runs.authority: a caller-supplied string on a store row, where host authority was granted once at connection level rather than per message (S00 finding 2), and hook/operator were never minted by any Forge code path at all. Canonical authority is kernel-asserted per turn. See globalRules R2.

fields.note: Same defect as runs.close_ledger_hash: computed by the process that wrote the ledger, so it is integrity-at-capture, not tamper evidence. Retained verbatim for legacy readers; canonical integrity is ReceiptStore.verifyChain().
Absent in the S00 fixtures because no resident time-accounting service ran in that environment (S00-REPORT coverage gaps).

fields.reason: A caller-supplied failure.error_fingerprint bypasses derivation entirely (lib/budget.js:46-51), so a model caller chooses its own retry-budget key. Canonical retry fingerprints are derived host-side (S04 action 9) from observed effect data, never accepted from the caller.

fields.note: Superseded by policy/arcane-policy-v1.json.

recordTypes.preservedBehavior: resolveSession's retirement of the 'sole open run' heuristic (lib/core.js:209-212) is a STRONGER invariant than guessing and is preserved: an unbound session resolves to unbound, never to an inferred run.

recordTypes.note: Forge appends a NEW rubrics row on every verify() call (lib/core.js:119), so rubrics is an append-only history of gate snapshots. Legion's contract is versioned and amended (G10), not re-snapshotted; the bridge projects only the LATEST rubric per run and records the discarded snapshot count.

fields.note: Legacy ids are free strings; bridge assigns AC-<n> and records the correspondence.
NAME COLLISION: Forge's per-criterion 'execution_contract' is a check-invocation spec, NOT a Legion ExecutionContract (EC-#). Never conflate them.
hashValue(rubric); not a monotonic contract version, so it does NOT map to execution-contract-v1.version.
Caller-supplied, unvalidated shape (lib/core.js:184-186).
always 'pending' at write time.

Forge hardcodes authority='quarantine' here so a caller cannot self-approve memory promotion (lib/core.js:185). That is a STRONGER invariant than the surrounding code and is preserved: imported memory candidates are never auto-promoted.

recordTypes.note: S00 finding 1 in full force. The field LIST is a reasonable compatibility surface; the trust properties are absent. Every field below is compatibility-only or rejected: not one of them can ground a canonical effect receipt on its own.

fields.canonicalTarget: effect-receipt-v1.requestId (correspondence only, never reused as a canonical req_ handle)

fields.reason: Literal string 'forge-claude-hook'. A self-declared identity, not an authenticated one. effect-receipt-v1.authentication.issuerIdentity must be established by S03 verification, never copied from here.
digest('forge-claude-hook:v1') — a fixed, non-secret hash of a literal string. It is not a capability token and grants nothing.

fields.canonicalTarget: effect-receipt-v1.observed.effectClass (candidate only, subject to S04 reclassification)

fields.note: Preserved as a digest only (S03 action 9).
Never mapped straight to result='applied'; S04 classifies.

fields.reason: `hook:${sha256(receipt)}` computed by the same untrusted process that built the receipt (hooks/claude-code/tool-receipt.js:80): no secret key, no MAC, no signature. Imported ONLY as unauthenticated legacy metadata inside the envelope payload (S03 action 11). Presenting it to Arcane as authentication is rejected with ARC_AUTH_LEGACY_DIGEST.

recordTypes.note: The one legacy record type with a hard closed-schema validator at its boundary (validateObservableEvent, hooks/observable-event.js:31-46) and structurally content-free by design (content_ref_or_digest must be a sha256 digest). Its discipline is ADOPTED by the S04 host-event contract rather than replaced.

fields.reason: origin='host' here is a self-declared string on a telemetry record, not an authenticated channel property. Canonical origin is established by S03 verification of the transport, not read off the payload.

fields.note: Already digest-only; adopt the discipline verbatim.

vocabularyMappings.name: run.status
vocabularyMappings.note: See runs.status field note — close-decision row disambiguates COMPLETED vs FAILED_INVOCATION.

vocabularyMappings.name: claim.status
vocabularyMappings.note: 'supported' does not survive import — see claims.status disposition.

vocabularyMappings.name: check.authority / run.authority / evidence issuer authority
vocabularyMappings.reason: Canonical authority is kernel-asserted per turn. Legacy 'hook' and 'operator' were never minted by any Forge code path at all.

unresolvedPolicy: Empty by construction: S01 acceptance requires no unresolved legacy item that can affect signoff, authority, invalidation, or compatibility. Every field above carries a disposition; items whose canonical meaning is genuinely absent are dispositioned 'compatibility-only' or 'deprecated' rather than left unmapped, and every trust-bearing field is either 'canonical' with a named target or 'rejected' with a sourced reason.
knownLegacyDefectsNotReproduced: Dispatcher timeout bypass (lib/dispatcher.js:29-37): a handler exceeding its 1500ms slice is marked bypassed_delayed_verifier and the dispatcher CONTINUES. Arcane's pre-effect gate fails closed on unavailability instead (ARC_GATE_UNAVAILABLE, failClosed:true) — the legacy fail-open is not reproduced.
Unconditional trust from authority='host' + non-empty receipt string (lib/core.js:493-494,536-539). Closed by S04 ingestion, which requires structural validation plus S03 verification.
Caller-chosen retry/error fingerprints (lib/budget.js:46-51). Canonical fingerprints are derived host-side.
signature_or_mac self-hash presented as authentication (hooks/claude-code/tool-receipt.js:80). Rejected with ARC_AUTH_LEGACY_DIGEST.

README-vs-code invalidation gap (S00 finding 4): lockfile/worktree/external-revision invalidation was documented but never implemented. S05 builds it as new work; this map does not claim it as migrated.
